title: Lecture 4 - Master Theorem & Divide-and-Conquer MCQs
description: Midterm MCQs on concepts, mathematical reasoning and proof steps. No code tracing or code-analysis questions.
subject: Algorithm Analysis

questions.question: In T(n)=aT(n/b)+f(n), what does a represent?
options: The total cost of all tree levels.
questions.explanation: There are a recursive calls of size n/b each.

questions.question: What does f(n) represent in the Master form?
options: The final answer returned by the algorithm.
The non-recursive dividing and combining work.
The number of input elements only.
The recursive cost already represented by aT(n/b).
questions.correctAnswer: The non-recursive dividing and combining work.
questions.explanation: The recurrence separates recursive subproblem costs from work done outside those calls.

questions.question: Which requirements on the constants are part of the stated Master form?
options: a=n and b=n for all n
questions.explanation: The standard form assumes a fixed positive number of subproblems and a fixed shrink factor greater than 1.

questions.question: What is the comparison exponent d for T(n)=aT(n/b)+f(n)?
questions.explanation: The leaf count grows as n^(log_b a).

questions.question: For f(n)=Θ(n^k(log n)^p), which result holds when d=log_b a>k?
questions.explanation: A polynomially larger leaf exponent dominates any fixed logarithmic factor.

questions.question: If d=k and p=0, what does the balanced Master case give?
questions.explanation: Equal polynomial work per level adds one logarithmic factor.

questions.question: If d=k and f(n)=Θ(n^d log n), what is the solution?
questions.explanation: Here p=1>-1, so the generalized equal-exponent case increases p by 1.

questions.question: If d=k and p=-1, what is the generalized Master result?
questions.explanation: The reciprocal-log equal-exponent case yields a log log n factor.

questions.question: What is the tight solution of 4T(n/2)+n²/(log₂ n)², with a constant base case above n=1?
questions.explanation: d=log₂4=2=k and p=-2<-1, giving Θ(n²).

questions.question: What is the tight solution of T(n)=2T(n/2)+n?
questions.explanation: a=b=2 gives d=k=1 with p=0, so the equal case adds log n.

questions.question: What is the tight solution of T(n)=5T(n/2)+n²?
questions.explanation: log₂5≈2.322 is greater than 2; the leaves dominate.

questions.question: What is the tight solution of T(n)=12T(n/3)+n³?
questions.explanation: log₃12≈2.262<3; cubic non-recursive work dominates and satisfies regularity.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] For f(n)=n³ and a=12,b=3, which ratio verifies Case 3 regularity?
questions.explanation: 12(n/3)³=(4/9)n³, so the next level shrinks by a constant factor below 1.

questions.question: Which recurrence is not directly in the equal-size Master form with a fixed shrink factor b>1?
questions.explanation: Subtracting one is not dividing by a fixed constant greater than 1.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly names the divide-and-conquer phases?
questions.explanation: Break the problem into smaller instances, solve them, then combine their results.

questions.question: What input property is required by ordinary binary search?
options: The array is reverse-sorted while comparisons assume ascending order.
The array is sorted according to the search order.
The array has exactly two elements.
questions.correctAnswer: The array is sorted according to the search order.
questions.explanation: Ordering justifies discarding a half after comparing with the midpoint.

questions.question: Why is binary search's worst-case recurrence T(n)=T(n/2)+Θ(1), rather than 2T(n/2)+Θ(1)?
options: Only one half needs to be searched after the comparison.
Both halves are searched simultaneously at no cost.
questions.correctAnswer: Only one half needs to be searched after the comparison.
questions.explanation: The comparison identifies which half could contain the target.

questions.question: How do quicksort and merge sort primarily differ in dividing their input?
options: Quicksort partitions by pivot-relative values; merge sort splits by positions.
Both must always split into equal-value groups.
Quicksort first fully sorts the whole array.
Merge sort requires a random pivot.
questions.correctAnswer: Quicksort partitions by pivot-relative values; merge sort splits by positions.
questions.explanation: Value-based partitioning can be unbalanced; the standard merge-sort position split is balanced.

questions.question: Which recurrence describes quicksort with a repeated extreme pivot and linear partition work?
questions.explanation: Only one nonempty side of size n-1 remains, while partitioning still scans the current input.

questions.question: What is the arithmetic cost of multiplying an m×n matrix by an n×l matrix classically?
questions.explanation: Each of ml result entries needs a length-n dot product.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] Why does naive recursive square-matrix multiplication have eight subproducts, not four?
options: Each of four output quadrants is the sum of two matrix products.
A square matrix always has eight entries.
Each output quadrant requires no multiplication.
Every divide-and-conquer recurrence must use eight calls.
questions.correctAnswer: Each of four output quadrants is the sum of two matrix products.
questions.explanation: The block multiplication equations require 2 products for each of 4 quadrants.

questions.question: What is the tight time of T(n)=8T(n/2)+Θ(n²)?
questions.explanation: d=log₂8=3>2, so the leaf term is cubic.

questions.question: Why is Strassen asymptotically faster than naive recursive matrix multiplication?
options: It replaces all recursion with a single constant-time step.
It multiplies only one pair of scalar entries.
It reduces eight half-size products to seven while keeping Θ(n²) extra arithmetic per call.
questions.correctAnswer: It reduces eight half-size products to seven while keeping Θ(n²) extra arithmetic per call.
questions.explanation: The recurrence becomes 7T(n/2)+Θ(n²), with exponent log₂7≈2.807 rather than 3.

questions.question: Which standard sorting choice combines stable Θ(n log n) time with Θ(n) auxiliary array storage?
options: Insertion sort with quadratic worst time.
questions.explanation: The lecture's merge sort is stable with consistent tie handling and needs temporary arrays.

questions.question: Which statement correctly qualifies the phrase "in-place quicksort"?
options: It guarantees Θ(n log n) worst-case time.
Its recursion stack is always Θ(1).
Its partition can be in-place while recursive calls still use stack memory.
questions.correctAnswer: Its partition can be in-place while recursive calls still use stack memory.
questions.explanation: In-place partitioning does not imply a zero-cost stack; straightforward worst-case recursion can be linear in depth.
